pass_a_gloss: [...] for indeed not as we do do they think the things below, but in certain unspeakable heights of thoughts the highest powers have their own mind. And of good speech also is their mouth. For they glorify also this from exchange, not, as I think, because of being weary, but rather yielding the honours to one another, and giving the glorifications as gifts in turn. For all the things above are in order. And saying thrice the 'Holy', they close the glorification into the 'Lord Sabaoth', setting the holy Trinity in one nature of Godhead. For we say confessedly that the Father subsists; and thus also the Son and the Holy Spirit. And no account cuts each of those named into natural otherness, but in three hypostases one Godhead is understood. And through the holy Seraphim themselves this has been witnessed to us, who also say all the earth is full of his glory, proclaiming beforehand the things to be, and announcing beforehand the mystery of the economy that came about through Christ. For before the Word became flesh, the destroying demon, the dragon, the apostate, ruled over the [world] under heaven. And the creation was worshipped beside the one who created and Maker; but since the only-begotten Word of God became man, all the earth has been filled with his glory. For every knee will bend to him, and every tribe, and tongues will confess, and will serve him, according to what is written. And the blessed David cried this out beforehand in spirit; for he said: All the nations as many as you made will come, and will worship before you, Lord. This indeed has been fulfilled, the multitude from nations having been called; and all worshipping the one who for us became as we are, but remained for himself above all. [Lemma, Isaiah 6:4:] And the lintel was lifted from the voice with which they had cried, and the house was filled with smoke. For the prophet had beheld the Lord Sabaoth sitting upon a throne high and lifted up, the holy Seraphim standing around in a circle, and praising him with unceasing glorifications. And he was affirming that the house is full of his glory. But now he says the lintel was lifted, and the house was filled with smoke, and from the voice with which the holy Seraphim had cried. Will we then say the voice became cause of the things that happened to the house? And yet how is it not very unseemly to choose to think these things? In what manner then will we approach the thoughts of the things set before us? Best and wisely. Before the becoming man and sojourn of our Saviour, Israel still administering the way of life in law unhindered and unrebuked, that famous temple in Jerusalem which Solomon built was full of the glory of God. For they were performing [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … as we do, think on the things below; rather, the highest powers keep their minds in certain unspeakable heights of thought. Their mouths too are given to praise. They give glory, and do so in turn, not because they grow weary, I think, but rather yielding the honor to one another and exchanging their praises as gifts. For all things above are in good order.

Saying “Holy” three times, they close the doxology with “Lord of hosts” (Isaiah 6:3), placing the holy Trinity in one nature of Godhead. For we say, as all confess, that the Father truly subsists, and so too the Son and the Holy Spirit. Yet no reasoning divides each of those named into a difference of nature; one Godhead is understood in three hypostases.

This is attested to us by the holy Seraphim themselves, who also say that the whole earth is full of his glory (Isaiah 6:3), foretelling what was to come and announcing beforehand the mystery of the saving plan carried out through Christ. Before the Word became flesh, the destroying demon, the dragon, the apostate, held sway over all that is under heaven, and the creation was worshiped in place of the Creator and Maker (Romans 1:25). But since the only-begotten Word of God became man, the whole earth has been filled with his glory.

For every knee will bow to him, and every tribe and tongue will confess him and serve him, as it is written (Isaiah 45:23; Philippians 2:10–11; Daniel 7:14). Blessed David also cried this out beforehand in the Spirit, for he said: “All the nations you have made will come and worship before you, O Lord” (Psalm 86:9). This has been fulfilled now that the multitude from the nations has been called, and all worship him who for our sake became as we are, yet in himself remained above all.
“And the lintel was lifted up at the voice with which they cried, and the house was filled with smoke” (Isaiah 6:4).

The prophet had seen the Lord of hosts sitting on a throne high and lifted up, with the holy Seraphim standing in a circle around him and praising him with unceasing doxologies; and he affirmed that the house was full of his glory (Isaiah 6:1–3). But now he says that the lintel was lifted up and the house filled with smoke, and this at the voice with which the holy Seraphim cried out.

Shall we then say that the voice was the cause of what happened to the house? Yet surely it would be most unseemly to choose to think so. How, then, shall we approach the meaning of the passage before us? In the best and wisest way.

choices.why: The Word made man remains God above all.
Cyril rejects a literal reading of the voice lifting the lintel.
